preamble: Glide formation turns the high front vowel [i] into the palatal glide [j] when it stands before another vowel, removing the hiatus. It was a general change from Classical Latin to Proto-Romance, is a productive synchronic rule of French, and is a regular rule of Sanskrit vowel sandhi.

examples.note: Unstressed front vowels in hiatus became /j/; the resulting /lj/ later gave Italian figlio /ʎ/ and Spanish hijo.
Synchronic glide formation before the vowel-initial infinitive ending; blocked after obstruent + liquid clusters.
External vowel sandhi: final i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel.

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Phonological changes from Classical Latin to Proto-Romance. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_changes_from_Classical_Latin_to_Proto-Romance
